title: Cocycle description and collapse of the Grothendieck left edge
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be a composable pair of left exact additive functors between Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-composite-acyclicity], with $F$ sending injectives to $G$-acyclics. Let $X\in\mathcal A$ and let $X\to I^\bullet$ be an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Under the natural derived-functor identifications $R^n(G\circ F)(X)\cong H^n(G(F(I^\bullet)))$ and $R^nF(X)\cong H^n(F(I^\bullet))$ [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], the left edge map of [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] is the morphism $$H^n(G(F(I^\bullet)))\longrightarrow G(H^n(F(I^\bullet)))$$ induced by taking a degree-$n$ cocycle in $G(F(I^\bullet))$, regarding it by left exactness of $G$ as a section of $G(\ker(F(I^n)\to F(I^{n+1})))$, and applying $G$ to the quotient morphism $\ker(F(I^n)\to F(I^{n+1}))\to H^n(F(I^\bullet))$. In particular, if $R^pG(R^qF(X))=0$ for all $p>0$ and all $q\geq0$, this left edge map is an isomorphism in every degree: the first-quadrant spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck] has a finite, exhaustive, separated decreasing filtration of each abutment object, and [lem-sp-edge-collapse] applies to its exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple] and convergence [def-sp-convergence].

proof.text: Choose the stated injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$. By [def-sp-injective-resolutions], [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], and the definition of right derived functors in [def-sp-left-exact-additive], applying $F$ and then $G$ to this resolution computes $R^n(G\circ F)(X)$ as $H^n(G(F(I^\bullet)))$, while $R^nF(X)$ is computed as $H^n(F(I^\bullet))$. Thus a degree-$n$ class on the source of the left edge can be represented by a cocycle in $G(F(I^n))$.

Choose a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $C^{\bullet,\bullet}$ of the bounded-below complex $F(I^\bullet)$ as in [thm-sp-if-e1], and form $D^{p,q}=G(C^{p,q})$. By [lem-pc-grothendieck-ss-double-complex-model], the Grothendieck spectral sequence is the first filtration spectral sequence of this double complex, with abutment identified through $H^n(G(F(I^\bullet)))$. In the filtration [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences], $F^0H^n=H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ and $F^1H^n$ is the first filtration step, so the edge is explicitly $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)\twoheadrightarrow F^0H^n/F^1H^n=E_\infty^{0,n}\hookrightarrow E_2^{0,n}=G(H^n(F(I^\bullet)))$. On a cocycle represented by $s\in G(F(I^n))$, the augmentation $G(F(I^q))\to G(C^{\bullet,q})$ is a quasi-isomorphism onto each row (the row $C^{\bullet,q}$ is an injective resolution of $F(I^q)$ by [thm-sp-if-e1]) because $F(I^q)$ is $G$-acyclic; hence this comparison sends $[s]$ to the corresponding total-complex class. Writing $Z^n=\ker(F(I^n)\to F(I^{n+1}))$, the $p=0$ column identifies the quotient map with $G$ applied to $Z^n\to H^n(F(I^\bullet))$, since left exactness gives $\ker(GF(I^n)\to GF(I^{n+1}))=G(Z^n)$. The edge is the left edge by [lem-pc-grothendieck-ss-double-complex-model] (and its abstract direction is [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps]); [lem-sp-derived-well-defined] gives independence of the resolution.

By [lem-pc-grothendieck-ss-double-complex-model], the Grothendieck spectral sequence is the first filtration spectral sequence of the double complex and has $E_2^{p,q}=R^pG(R^qF(X))$. Its filtration is the finite exhaustive separated filtration of $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ supplied by [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences], and its bigraded exact couple is the one defined in [def-sp-exact-couple], with convergence as in [def-sp-convergence]. If $R^pG(R^qF(X))=0$ for every $p>0$ and $q$, all entries outside the $p=0$ column vanish already on $E_2$. Applying [lem-sp-edge-collapse] to this exact couple gives $E_\infty=E_2$ and makes the edge map $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)\to E_2^{0,n}=G(R^nF(X))$ an isomorphism. The model node identifies this edge with the left edge of [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps], and Step 2 identifies it with the displayed cocycle morphism.
